payload.description:
events.jsonl truncation actively losing live writes today (2026-08-26), not just a historical incident -- fgos doctor's events-jsonl-not-truncated check (added by tsk-cgg) is failing right now

Description:
Live evidence from this session (writer 80f8fa1e-124f-480b-9b98-e4e4838f560a), not a repeat of the closed docs/history/events-jsonl-git-tracked-truncation/ investigation:

1. .fgos/events.jsonl's tip is frozen at seq 24759, ts 2026-08-26T00:19:32Z -- over 13 hours stale at time of observation, despite the truncation-guard's own last-recorded mark being seq 24765 (proof forward progress existed and was reverted).
2. This session ran `fgos submit` + `fgos pick` for a new item (tsk-67t2) at 2026-08-26T13:43:02-13:43:08Z -- both succeeded, and `fgos list --id tsk-67t2` confirmed it fully readable (claim data, worktree, branch fgw/tsk-67t2) as late as 13:43:19Z.
3. By ~13:53Z (next fgos call, `fgos handoff`) the item had vanished completely: `fgos list --id tsk-67t2` and `fgos list --all` both return not-found, grep -rl "tsk-67t2" across every .fgos/events/*.jsonl shard returns zero hits, and no shard file matching this session's own writer id exists anywhere under .fgos/events/. Only an orphaned .fgos/runtime/claims/tsk-67t2.json and the git branch fgw/tsk-67t2 remain.
4. fgos doctor's events-jsonl-not-truncated check fails with reason:regressed, naming 8 affected files (events.jsonl + 8 shards), all pointing at the same documented cause class (docs/how-to/resolve-an-events-jsonl-truncation.md): a raw git stash/checkout--/reset --hard/clean run directly against the shared, git-tracked main checkout while .fgos/events.jsonl had live uncommitted appends.

Not resolved by this report: which session/process actually ran the destructive git command -- no reflog/history access from a worktree-isolated session to identify the actor. The mechanism class is documented and precedented; this item's evidence is that it recurred live today and is actively eating fresh, just-created work-item state, not only old history.

Scope: investigate the actual recurring source (likely an autonomous loop -- merge-loop/cleanup-loop/retro-loop -- or another concurrent session running a raw git command on the main checkout instead of fgos main-checkout-reset), then apply the runbook's human-run re-baseline step, then decide whether the guard needs to become a hard pre-flight block on fgos submit/pick (not just a doctor-time detector) given it is now confirmed to silently eat freshly-created items, not just old history.

Verify:
fgos doctor's events-jsonl-not-truncated check passes after re-baseline AND after the recurring source is identified and fixed (not just re-baselined blind) -- re-baselining alone without root-causing the actor would silently repeat this same live data loss.

payload.title: Orphaned runtime claim + deterministic generateId collision has no recovery command -- discovered…
payload.description:
Orphaned runtime claim + deterministic generateId collision has no recovery command -- discovered while recovering from tsk-46v's events.jsonl truncation

Description:
While redoing the tsk-67t2 spike after its events were lost to the events.jsonl truncation (tsk-46v), resubmitting the identical task text reproduced the identical item id -- generateId (src/intake/classify.mjs:124) hashes only the title, and the durable work record for tsk-67t2 no longer existed post-truncation so the collision check (existingIds) didn't block it. But .fgos/runtime/claims/tsk-67t2.json (the orphaned claim from the original, now-vanished, submit+pick) still existed and IS keyed by that same id -- fgos pick tsk-67t2 refused with 'already claimed by claimId clm-...', even though fgos list --id tsk-67t2 showed a fresh work.status:todo record with no matching active claim from the durable event log's own point of view.

This is a durable-state vs ephemeral-claim-state divergence with no documented or mechanical recovery path:
- docs/how-to/recover-a-stuck-doing-claim-after-worktree-creation-failure.md does not cover it -- that runbook is for status:doing with a missing worktree; this case is status:todo (or any non-doing durable status) with a claim file that still thinks it's held.
- src/state/runtime-coordination.mjs's acquireClaim (via src/runner/claim-port.mjs, isReclaimEligible/claim-liveness.mjs) only reclaims a stale claim by WORKTREE ACTIVITY LIVENESS threshold -- it has no path that checks 'does this claim's own id even still have a matching durable status that would justify the claim' before refusing.

Workaround used (not a fix): reworded the resubmit's title text so generateId produced a different, non-colliding id (tsk-3rn), sidestepping the collision entirely rather than clearing the orphaned claim.

Scope: decide whether acquireClaim/isReclaimEligible should also reclaim when the durable work.status no longer supports the existing claim record (e.g. status is todo/nonexistent while a claim file says otherwise), or whether a dedicated recovery verb/doc is the right shape instead -- similar in spirit to /fgOS:unlock but for a per-item claim record rather than the main-checkout lock.

Verify:
A reproducing test or manual repro (submit -> pick -> simulate durable-state loss e.g. via a direct events.jsonl edit in a throwaway fixture -> resubmit identical title -> pick) demonstrates the fix either auto-reclaims or gives a clear, documented recovery command -- not a silent 'already claimed' refusal with no path forward.
